summary: Potential session cookie capture following third-party contractor file-upload integration
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 at ~09:40 UTC, the Security Monitoring pipeline raised anomalous session reuse events tied to a small set of engineer accounts after a vendor contractor uploaded test binaries via the contracted file-upload proxy. Impact: 6 engineer sessions showed short-lived access from IPs unrelated to known corporate ranges; two sessions performed read-only requests to internal monitoring endpoints. No data exfiltration confirmed; investigation in progress.

Environment: Production (VPC private upload proxy in us-east-1) with vendor-facing S3-compatible upload endpoint managed by third-party contractor. Affected service: internal dev tooling and session token handling via cookie-based auth used by the console.

Observed behavior: the file upload flow responds with a 302 redirect to a callback URL. A subset of logged requests indicate that the redirect included an app-level Set-Cookie header coming from a proxy error path, and an external IP subsequently presented those cookies to the console API. Hypothesis: misconfigured proxy or vendor test harness echoed an authenticated Set-Cookie header into the public redirect response, enabling session reuse if the redirect URL was followed by an external actor.

Immediate customer impact: internal only. No customer tenant access observed at this time.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Engineer A authenticates to console (cookie-based session).
2) Engineer A initiates file upload to vendor proxy via /upload/initiate endpoint.
3) Vendor proxy issues a 302 redirect to contractor callback with a transient upload token.
4) In error path, proxy erroneously returns Set-Cookie: session=<session_value> header in redirect response (observed in logs).
5) External IP follows redirect and reuses cookie to call console API, resulting in apparent session reuse from unfamiliar IP.
logs: 2026-03-12T09:39:58Z proxy-1 ERROR redirect-handling: emitted Set-Cookie for session ID=*** (path=/; HttpOnly) while handling vendor-callback; req_id=abc123
2026-03-12T09:40:11Z auth-api INFO login: session validated for user=devops_eng from ip=54.82.10.21; session_id=***; originating_ip=157.52.8.9 (upload-proxy)
2026-03-12T09:40:13Z sec-monitor ALERT session-anomaly: simultaneous-active-sessions user=devops_eng sessions=2 src_ips=[54.82.10.21,12.45.67.89] correlation_score=0.78
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Jonah Park (sec-ops): Initial alert came in from sec-monitor. Flagged for immediate triage. Notifying SRE and Vendor ops.
2026-03-12 10:22 - Devon Chen (SRE): Querying upload proxy logs and blocking the contractor's test harness IP ranges at the edge while we validate. Temporary rule applied.

2026-03-12 11:00 - Maria Lopez (Vendor ops): Vendor confirms they were running an automated integration test and may have used an internal callback URL; they are pausing runs and providing full request traces.

2026-03-12 14:30 - Ava Martinez (Sec Eng): Performed token validation and confirmed 6 sessions had ephemeral reuse markers; no long-lived tokens issued. Preparing token rotation plan for affected principals.

2026-03-14 09:15 - Devon Chen (SRE): Edge rule remains in place. Vendor provided patched proxy code; we have a staging PR exercising redirect path. Need coordination for staged rollout and rotating cookies for implicated users.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Upload proxy error path incorrectly copies incoming upstream Set-Cookie headers to redirect responses. Confirmed by log snippet with 'emitted Set-Cookie' entry.

Hypothesis B: Contractor test harness used a browser automation that replayed redirect URLs to external IPs; may be accidental leak rather than malicious intent. Vendor traces show automated CI job from contractor-eu-2 during window.

Token analysis: All implicated session IDs expired within 10 minutes and were non-refreshable; tokens were not used for privileged write operations. No cross-account resource access found in query through 2026-03-12T12:00Z.
Network analysis: External IP 12.45.67.89 maps to contractor test cluster; additional IPs from cloud provider were observed but matched vendor-owned ranges per RIPE lookups.

Risk determination: Medium (internal accounts only) -> escalating due to potential for cookie leakage in redirect paths. Recommend immediate containment plus full token rotation for affected principals.
mitigation_steps_taken: 1) Blocked vendor-run CI IP ranges at edge load-balancer (WAF rule) — applied 2026-03-12T10:30Z.
2) Disabled public redirects for vendor uploads; switched to signed upload callbacks that don't pass Set-Cookie headers — temporary config applied 2026-03-12T11:05Z.
3) Rotated session cookies for 6 affected engineers and forced re-login; increased monitoring for 72h.
4) Requested vendor patch to proxy code to ensure no Set-Cookie header propagation in redirect responses; vendor submitted PR and test traces 2026-03-13.
5) Created temporary runbook section for vendor upload handling and redirect validation.
resolution: Partial mitigation complete: vendor test runs paused, WAF blocks in place, affected sessions rotated, and vendor patch validated in staging. Next steps: plan staged rollout of patched proxy (canary in eu-west then us-east), audit all redirect response code paths across upload proxies, and add unit/integration tests to prevent Set-Cookie propagation. Final closure pending completion of rollout and 7-day clean monitoring window.
follow_up_actions: Schedule canary rollout with SRE and Vendor Ops (owner: Devon Chen) — target week of 2026-03-16.
Add automated test that asserts redirect responses do not include Set-Cookie headers (owner: Platform QA).
Expand sec-monitor rule to detect Set-Cookie headers in any redirect response originating from internal proxies (owner: Sec Eng).
Deliver vendor audit checklist requiring signed callback flow and no cookie-bearing headers (owner: Vendor Risk).
notes: This ticket is internal. Coordinate communication to affected engineers via #sec-ops and #sre. No external customer notifications at this time.
